Where a mushroom fruits is as telling as what it looks like. A species
named in a guide without its tree is half a species.

Chanterelles follow beech and oak leaf litter and show up where the
moss thins. Porcini keep to spruce and chestnut, often on a slope where
the soil drains and warms. Field mushrooms want grazed pasture and
short grass, not the deep shade, and they fruit in rings a season can
predict.

Learn three habitats properly before chasing a long list: the tree, the
soil, and what the ground does after rain. A basket of names is worth
less than one wood you know in every month of a bad season.
